title: §4.2 belt-and-braces guard checks the escaped wire form only for referee_ip/UA — form_token/payload_ref escaped detection is vacuous
detail: The guard's own comment claims "both forms are checked", but escaped forms (the only wire form for keys inside the JSON-string result field) exist only for referee_ip/referee_user_agent. A corrupt stored result containing "form_token" or "payload_ref" keys would ship as \"form_token\" and pass the guard; the negative-control test feeds those two markers only in the unescaped top-level form the encoder can never emit, and the guard is never invoked at runtime (test-only), so the "re-verifies the serialized payload" claim overstates its reach.
recommended_fix: Add "\\\"form_token\\\"" and "\\\"payload_ref\\\"" to the markers list and extend verify_payload_guard_detects_internal_markers_test with the escaped result-string forms.

title: Unknown outcome value serialises as "unreachable" on the wire while unknown status renders "failed" — the encoder can fabricate a state
detail: outcome_from_string's total fallback (_ -> OutcomeUnreachable, shared:215) means any future enum value (v2 voice outcomes) would surface as outcome "unreachable" on a row whose status decodes "failed" — a fabricated factual claim (the referee wasn't reached), not an inert render like the status fallback. The PR's self-review #3 standard (hooks and status never diverge) holds for status/hooks but the outcome field can contradict the same row's render during an expand window.
recommended_fix: In encode_reference_call, map unrecognised outcome strings to None (absent) instead of round-tripping outcome_from_string's OutcomeUnreachable fallback, so the wire never asserts an unreachable state the row did not reach.
